description: SentimentMarker scoring model: one rule set, named vocabularies. Canonical source; tools/build-lexicon.js generates the browser assets from it.

neutralPhrases.note: "financial stability" names a policy topic, not a sentiment: stability is not scored inside it.

sources.licence: The finance vocabulary derives from the Loughran-McDonald Master Dictionary, which its authors (Tim Loughran and Bill McDonald, University of Notre Dame) make available free of charge for non-commercial / academic use only; commercial use requires a licence from the authors (https://sraf.nd.edu/loughranmcdonald-master-dictionary/). Strengths come from the VADER lexicon (C.J. Hutto and Eric Gilbert), MIT licence. The general vocabulary is SentimentMarker's own hand-written demo list.

loughranMcDonald.licence: Free for non-commercial / academic use only; commercial use requires a licence from the authors (Tim Loughran and Bill McDonald).
loughranMcDonald.name: Loughran-McDonald Master Dictionary
loughranMcDonald.version: as shipped in pysentiment2 0.1.1 (the package does not state the LM release)

finance.origin: Loughran-McDonald polarity x VADER strength, built by tools/build_finance_vocab.py.

general.origin: Hand-written demo list (the original in-browser dictionary).

finance.description: Loughran-McDonald decides polarity, VADER supplies strength (else ±1.5); strongly polarised VADER-only words (|score| >= 2.5) are added. No suffix fallback: it produced false matches such as goods -> good and bridging -> bridge.
finance.label: Finance dictionary (LM × VADER)

general.description: Small general-purpose English list plus a Chinese starter set; tolerant suffix fallback.
general.label: General dictionary
